title: Chi-Square Test with SciPy
learning_objectives: Run a goodness-of-fit test with scipy.stats.chisquare
Interpret a p-value and compare it with a significance level
Relate the p-value to the chi-square distribution's upper tail
hints: Validate the inputs as in the hand-written test, plus `0 < alpha < 1`.
`expected = [total * p for p in probs]`; then `result = stats.chisquare(observed, f_exp=expected)`.
Return `float(result.statistic)`, `float(result.pvalue)`, `len(observed) - 1` and the comparison with alpha.

failure_feedback.advice: Pass expected counts (total × p), not probabilities, as f_exp.
Convert NumPy results with float(...); the comparison gives a bool.
Validate before calling SciPy, including alpha.
